epics.title: Personal AI Regulatory Assistant & GOST Order Generator
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator, instructor, or resident needs regulatory guidance or administrative drafts, I want an AI assistant grounded in institutional knowledge and a one-click GOST R 7.0.97-2016 .docx order generator, so that official administrative tasks are executed accurately in seconds.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of generated GOST DOCX documents conform to Times New Roman 14pt typography declared in template_registry.json
epics.tocConstraintRef: Hardcoded Pt(12)/Pt(13)/Pt(9)/Pt(10) font sizes in compile_session_to_docx
requirements: R1: Update compile_session_to_docx in crie_document_engine.py so body paragraphs, requisites, preamble, actions, signatures, headers, and approval/visa blocks use Times New Roman 14pt aligned with GOST R 7.0.97-2016 and the gost_font declaration in data/templates/template_registry.json.

R2: Verify generated DOCX paragraph and run XML styling in automated unit/integration tests to ensure zero hardcoded Pt(12), Pt(13), Pt(10), or Pt(9) overrides remain in compile_session_to_docx output.

slices.title: Enforce Times New Roman 14pt in compile_session_to_docx
slices.jtbd: When implementing GOST R 7.0.97-2016 typography compliance for this epic, I want compile_session_to_docx in crie_document_engine.py and its tests updated to emit Times New Roman 14pt across document elements, so that generated DOCX orders satisfy the declared GOST font specification.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a document session compiled via compile_session_to_docx in crie_document_engine.py, When body paragraphs, requisites, preamble, actions, title/command headers, signatures, and approval/visa blocks are rendered, Then all text runs use Times New Roman 14pt matching data/templates/template_registry.json.
Given the updated compile_session_to_docx implementation, When pytest executes the DOCX typography unit and integration assertions against a generated order file, Then all assertions confirm Pt(14) font sizing and pass without skipped checks.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Font-size helper and run formatting calls inside crie_document_engine.py
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 non-14pt font-size overrides detected across compiled DOCX runs

epics.title: GOST Admission Order Template Study-Form & Funding-Source Clauses
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator generates a residency or postgraduate admission order from GOST templates, I want the operative clause to automatically include exact regulatory wording for full-time study form and federal-budget vs. paid-contract funding from admission_records, so that generated orders are legally complete without manual editing.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of TPL-01 residency admission orders include required study-form and funding-source tokens
epics.tocConstraintRef: Missing study-form token in TPL-01 required_tokens within data/templates/template_registry.json
requirements: R1: Add a required study-form token (e.g., STUDY_FORM) to TPL-01 required_tokens in data/templates/template_registry.json alongside BUDGET_TYPE and ensure template binding/rendering populates both study form and funding source.
R2: Add automated unit/integration test coverage verifying TPL-01 metadata completeness and rendered admission order text containing both study form and financing source.

slices.title: Add study-form token to TPL-01 residency admission template
slices.jtbd: When implementing complete admission-order template parameters for this epic, I want TPL-01 in data/templates/template_registry.json and its rendering path updated to require and substitute the study-form parameter alongside BUDGET_TYPE, so that generated residency admission orders include both study form and funding source.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given template TPL-01 in data/templates/template_registry.json, When required_tokens and template rendering logic are inspected, Then TPL-01 declares a study-form parameter alongside ORD_ID, FULL_NAME, SPECIALTY_CODE, SPECIALTY_NAME, BUDGET_TYPE, ORDER_NUMBER, and DATE and binds it into generated order clauses.
Given automated template registry and document generation tests, When TPL-01 is loaded and compiled with study-form and funding-source values, Then all assertions pass confirming both clauses appear in the generated output.
slices.tocConstraintRef: TPL-01 schema definition and token substitution in crie_template_manager.py
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% required_tokens validation pass rate for TPL-01 across test fixtures

epics.title: Knowledge-First PR Diff Inspection Gate & Unverified PR Audit
epics.jtbd: When repository maintainers and automated review agents evaluate pull requests for merge readiness, I want every approval verdict backed by inspected diff evidence and verified acceptance/security checks rather than assumption when diffs are absent, so that unverified or incomplete PRs never receive false-green approvals.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% false-green approvals emitted when PR diffs or target deliverables are absent from review context
epics.tocConstraintRef: Lenient approval verdicts issued without diff inspection across PRs #407, #408, #413, and #415-#421
requirements: R1: Audit the current product codebase against the uninspected PR targets referenced in Findings 1-5 (PRs #407, #408, #413, #415, #416, #417, #418, #419, #420, #421, including checks for crie_persistent_memory.py, crie_normative_knowledge.py, kcp_parameters schema/Order #824 seed values, SQLite admission/PDF parser tables, security checks, and committed build artifacts) and document verified vs. missing deliverables in a committed audit report.

R2: Define and enforce the binary knowledge-first refusal rule requiring REJECT/BLOCK whenever PR diffs or target files are absent or uninspectable in review context, prohibiting lenient approval alongside medium/high missing-diff concerns.

R3: Verify and remediate any product-tree acceptance, idempotency, or artifact-hygiene gaps uncovered during inspection of the existing PR deliverables in the repository without altering forbidden .eneik/ or .github/ pipeline files.

R4: Add automated QA/integration tests verifying repository integrity invariants (presence/importability of expected modules, schema/seed idempotency where present, absence of unintended committed build artifacts, and automated gate failure when required diff/deliverable evidence is missing).

slices.title: Audit uninspected PR deliverables and formalize knowledge-first gate
slices.jtbd: When implementing merge-hygiene remediation for this epic, I want a concrete diff-and-deliverable audit of PRs #407, #408, #413, and #415-#421 recorded in docs/verification/pr-diff-audit-report.md alongside any required product-tree hygiene fixes, so that missing diffs are explicitly blocked and verified deliverables are documented.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the repository working tree and the target scope of PRs #407, #408, #413, #415, #416, #417, #418, #419, #420, and #421, When each PR's claimed files, SQLite schemas, Order #824 seed values, PDF parser tables, security checks, and build-artifact status are inspected, Then docs/verification/pr-diff-audit-report.md records an explicit binary PASS or BLOCKED_MISSING_DIFF/DELIVERABLE status for every PR.
Given the knowledge-first gate policy in docs/verification/pr-diff-audit-report.md, When a PR diff or target file is absent or uninspectable in review context, Then the documented refusal protocol requires rejecting/blocking approval until diff evidence, security checks, and acceptance verification are supplied.
Given any product-tree artifact hygiene or code defects surfaced in inspected files during the audit, When fixes are applied within the allowed product source scope, Then no .eneik/, .github/, or .env files are modified.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Cross-PR inventory reconciliation against current repository tree
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of 10 flagged PRs (#407, #408, #413, #415-#421) audited with explicit binary evidence status

slices.title: Add automated QA verification suite for PR deliverables and diff-gate invariants
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA verification for this epic, I want an automated pytest suite validating deliverable presence, SQLite/seed idempotency where applicable, build-artifact cleanliness, and strict failure on missing evidence, so that false-green merge verdicts cannot recur unnoticed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new pytest module in tests/, When unit tests evaluate the knowledge-first verification helper against mocked complete vs. missing-diff review contexts, Then missing-diff contexts strictly return reject/block and never approve.
Given integration checks in the same pytest suite against the repository tree, When checks inspect for unintended build artifacts, verify normative/template/document invariants, and validate any present PR target modules, Then all assertions run deterministically and pass without skipped or relaxed conditions.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Automated assertion coverage of absent vs. present deliverable states in pytest
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% deterministic pass rate on verification gate unit and repository integration tests
